publications.assertionSummary: Isaac Gurney (c. 1643, uncertain): surfaces in 1666–67 Middlesex/Suffolk court records; almost certainly this family's Isaac though no record states parentage.

incoming.explanation: The court records establish the person Isacke Gurney but state no parentage, so their bearing on the identification is indirect.

outgoing.explanation: Isaac is the uncertain sixth member; the by-elimination identification qualifies the roster's completeness.

finding.shortLabel: Isaac (c. 1643) most plausibly John-1's son, by elimination (moderate)
finding.statement: The young Isacke Gurney of the 1663/4–1667 colonial court records is most plausibly John Gurney-1's son: no record states his parentage, but an Isaac born c. 1643 needs a father of John's generation, and the only other regional Gurney male, Richard (G12, b. c. 1630–34), was himself a child in 1643 — a moderate identification the dedicated subject file still holds cautiously as a distinct person.

finding.shortLabel: Isacke Gurney court cluster: Scituate 1663/4; Suffolk file 792, 1667

sources.alignmentNote: Two colonial court records of a young Isacke Gurney (Scituate 1663/4; Medford/Boston 1667); neither states parentage. Full treatment on research/people/isaac-gurney-scituate-boston.md.
sources.excerpt: Isacke Gurney, for pilfering and other disorderly liueing, was sentenced by the Court to bee whipt
sources.locator: Plymouth Court Orders 1661–1668 images 35, 37 (arks 3:1:3Q9M-C9BJ-NW1P-1, 3:1:3Q9M-C9BJ-NW15-5); Suffolk County Court Case Files 1666–1668 file no. 792 images 56–59 (arks 3:1:3Q9M-CSVR-R913-N, 3:1:3Q9M-CSVR-R91S-Y)

finding.statement: A young Isacke Gurney appears in a tight cluster of colonial court records — whipped for pilfering at Scituate (Plymouth court, 1 March 1663/4) and jailed for vagrancy and burglary at Medford, committed to the Boston prison under Daniel Gookin's warrant (Suffolk County court file no. 792, June 1667); neither record states his parentage.
